claims.claim_text: The Republican Party regards federalism as a cornerstone of the U.S. constitutional system.
The Republican Party regards every violation of U.S. state sovereignty by federal officials as harming individual Americans' liberties.
The Republican Party characterizes the U.S. Constitution as granting the federal government very few, specifically enumerated powers.

Under the Republican Party's account of the U.S. Tenth Amendment, powers not constitutionally delegated to the federal government and not constitutionally prohibited to the states are reserved to the states or the people.

Republicans condemn what they describe as the 2016 U.S. administration's unconstitutional expansion beyond enumerated powers through coercive intervention in state and local voter-ID, immigration, healthcare, land-use, mandated-curriculum and school-restroom policies.
Republicans pledge to restore what they regard as the proper balance and vertical separation of powers between the U.S. federal government and state governments.
Republicans encourage U.S. states to renew their traditional role in advancing the country through local and state innovation.
Republicans assess U.S. state governments as closest to and most reflective of the American people.
